correctness.rationale: The source's defining set and Gray-coordinate formula reconstruct two \(48\)-column blocks \(V\setminus S_1\) and \(V\setminus S_2\) in \(V=\mathbb F_2^6\), with \(\dim S_1=\dim S_2=4\) and \(\dim(S_1\cap S_2)=3\). For an \(r\)-subcode with annihilator \(W\), zero positions are exactly the columns in \(W\), giving support \(96-2^{7-r}+2^{\dim(W\cap S_1)}+2^{\dim(W\cap S_2)}\). Grassmann lower bounds plus explicit simultaneous witnesses prove the hierarchy. Exhaustive RREF enumeration of all \(2824\) positive-dimensional message subspaces gives the full spectra, and direct generator supports agree with the structural formula in every case. The \(r=1\) spectrum reproduces the source enumerator exactly.

originality.rationale: The primary article gives only ordinary weights for Example 4.4 and has no generalized-Hamming-weight or subcode-support discussion. The most relevant full-text SSWD construction found in prior literature requires deletion of a strictly nested chain of projective subspaces with strictly increasing dimensions; the present two deleted 4-spaces are distinct, non-nested, and intersect in dimension 3. Exact searches by source identifier, [96,6,48] parameters, hierarchy, Gray-image aliases, and support-distribution language found no same-object statement. A 2026 antiGriesmer paper remains a named residual risk because only its public abstract was available, but exact-parameter searches did not identify this code and its advertised framework centers on projective/simplex-complementary constructions whereas this generator is nonprojective.
residual_risks: The full text of the 2026 antiGriesmer paper was not available in the inspected public sources, so a hidden equivalent specialization there cannot be ruled out solely from its abstract.
An unindexed computation could contain the same finite higher-support census.
No general theorem for all source-family parameters is claimed.

value.rationale: The source presents Example 4.4 as a new distance-optimal near-Griesmer Gray image and records its complete ordinary weight enumerator. Generalized Hamming weights are the canonical higher-dimensional refinement of minimum distance, and the complete SSWD records substantially more support-incidence information than the one-dimensional enumerator. The exact six-level hierarchy and every subcode multiplicity expose the geometry created by two overlapping deleted 4-spaces, including new odd support layers in dimensions four and five. This is a natural complete invariant of a highlighted optimal example rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
